newsitem.title: USA: Xerox sees growth from products, controls.
newsitem.headline: Xerox sees growth from products, controls.

text.p: Xerox Corp expects double-digit earnings growth in 1997 and beyond from new products and cost controls, the company said.

"There are two key reasons underlying our optimism: we are focused on large segments of a huge market that is growing at more than 10 percent a year, and we have a pipeline filled with superior products and technology," Chief Executive Officer Paul A. Allaire told investors and securities analysts, the company said in a statement.
Reporters were not invited to the session.
"We expect these growth opportunities along with our continuing focus on productivity-driven expense controls will lead to double-digit earnings growth in 1997 and beyond," he said.
New digital black-and-white copiers to be introduced in mid-April will provide "better quality and reliability and will be more feature-rich than anything on the market," Allaire said.
"And, they will also be easily upgradeable to act as high-speed, robust printers on networks."
"This approach builds on the very successful DocuTech Production Publishing strategy of selling stand-alone products and subsequently upgrading them to the network."
Over the course of 1997, he said, additional digital black-and-white and color products and more than a dozen new light-lens copiers will be introduced.
"Our approach is to give customers the products they want, whether it's black-and-white or color, digital or light lens, stand-alone or networked," Allaire said.

He also said the company's strategy is to move its highly successful digital production publishing business up market, more and more into offset printing and graphic arts. Xerox now does $1.8 billion a year in this business, driven by the DocuTech family of products.

Color is now a $1 billion business for Xerox, up 59 percent last year, Allaire noted. He said the company's superior color technology should allow Xerox to capture an even greater share of the market.
The company said it would also expand its $1.3 billion outsourcing business to include a broad range of document services, including network services, consulting, software and Internet services.
"Document services will ultimately be our lead offering to customers in managing documents across the enterprise," Allaire said. "It's a big part of our future."
